_note: The Story of Prophet Yahya (John the Baptist), son of Zakariyya, drawn strictly from the Qur'an (Surahs Maryam, Al Imran, al-An'am, al-Anbiya). Verse text resolves from the loaded Qur'an. No figural imagery; summaries carry no Arabic script.

events.title: A Name Given by Allah
events.summary: Yaḥyā was the answer to his father's prayer — a boy whose name Allah Himself chose, one never given to anyone before him. The angels announced him to Zakariyya as 'confirming a word from Allah' — that is, bearing witness to ʿĪsā son of Maryam — and as noble, chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous.
events.why: Yaḥyā's life begins as a miracle and a witness: born to the aged and barren, named by Allah, and appointed to confirm the coming of ʿĪsā — the two cousins whose stories run side by side.

events.title: Wisdom as a Child
events.summary: 'O Yaḥyā, take the Scripture with determination.' And We gave him judgement and wisdom while yet a child — a gravity and understanding of the Book granted him in his earliest years.
events.why: Where prophethood usually comes with age, Yaḥyā is given the Scripture and sound judgement as a boy — a sign that Allah's gifts follow no human timetable.

media.caption: Schematic diagram of the setting — Wisdom as a Child.

events.title: Tenderness, Purity, and Duty
events.summary: And affection from Us, and purity; and he was God-fearing, and dutiful to his parents, and he was not arrogant or disobedient.
events.why: In a few words the Qur'an paints a whole character: a heart soft with compassion, a life kept pure, reverence for Allah, and gentleness with his parents — the portrait of the righteous soul.

media.caption: Schematic diagram of the setting — Tenderness, Purity, and Duty.

events.title: Peace Be Upon Him
events.summary: 'And peace be upon him the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive.' The same blessing the Qur'an pronounces over ʿĪsā is pronounced over Yaḥyā — over his birth, his death, and his resurrection.
events.why: The threefold peace crowns a life of purity and marks its end: Yaḥyā, who bore witness to the truth, is met with Allah's own greeting of peace at every threshold of his existence.

media.caption: Schematic diagram of the setting — Peace Be Upon Him.

paths.title: The Arc of Yaḥyā
paths.blurb: The child named by Allah and given wisdom young — tender, pure, and dutiful — over whom peace is pronounced at his birth, his death, and his rising.
